purpose: Fill the missing canonical MLP-PINN, GW-PINN, AV-PINN, and CI-PINN comparison requested for the DKAN shock study. This table is descriptive and separate from the v3 strong-20% confirmation.

variants.gw_pinn: same MLP with exponential-moving-average inverse gradient-norm balancing, clipped to [0.1, 10]
variants.av_pinn: same MLP with fixed artificial viscosity in the strong residual
variants.ci_pinn: same MLP with coupled strong, control-volume integral, entropy, and global-balance losses

common.architecture_fairness: All four PINN variants use exactly the same MLP architecture within each equation.
common.reporting: Report all seeds, median and range; no winner gate and no post-execution hyperparameter changes.

euler.problem: standard Sod tube at t=0.2 on [0,1]
metrics: geometric mean of density_l2, velocity_l2, pressure_l2

hybrid_context.comparison_role: Report the already-confirmed hybrid and fixed-MC/WENO or exact references in adjacent rows, but do not merge their supervised offline cost with PINN optimization time.
hybrid_context.claim_boundary: Canonical single-problem baselines do not extend the v3 parameter-scan claim and do not make the hybrid a PINN.

execution_outcome.interpretation: AV-PINN had the lowest state error among PINNs. CI-PINN improved several conservation/entropy metrics but did not improve state error. Fixed finite-volume MC and the hybrid were substantially more accurate on these shock problems.
